implementation_statement: Each SaaS service has one account, the owner's, with administrator rights; no other user accounts exist. Gap: a family member sometimes uses the laptop under the owner's account, and no one reviews which third-party apps are connected to the email and CRM accounts.
evidence: SaaS user lists (P07); laptop user accounts

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner-adviser holds every role. The qualified custodian holds client assets and runs its own fraud checks on money movement; its call to the client stopped the $36,000 wire request on 2026-06-18. POL-01 7.6 requires a callback to the phone number on file in the CRM before any money movement or change of bank instructions or client contact details. The outsourced compliance consultant does an annual compliance review on a sample of client files. Gap: the callback rule and its CRM field are due in use by 2026-09-30 (POAM-002).
evidence: Custodian money movement records; POL-01 7.6; POAM-002

implementation_statement: The laptop locks after 5 minutes idle and the phone after 1 minute; both need the password or passcode to unlock.

The IT consultant connects only through a remote-support tool that the owner starts for each session and watches. Gap: allowed remote access and connection rules were not written down before this assessment.
The owner takes compliance continuing education only. The owner will complete an annual security awareness course for small financial firms and subscribe to monthly security reminders by 2026-11-30.
Planned: the annual course must cover business email compromise, fake payment requests, and impersonation of clients and the custodian. Until then the callback rule (POL-01 7.6) is the main defense.
The custodian portal, email suite, CRM, and portfolio platform log sign-ins and key actions. The email plan keeps sign-in history for 30 days.
evidence: Vendor admin consoles; SOC 2 report for SYS-02 (P09)

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: No one has reviewed sign-in history, mailbox forwarding rules, or platform activity. An unrecognized forwarding rule was found on 2026-07-15 and deleted. Starting 2026-10, the owner reviews sign-ins, forwarding rules, connected apps, and new money movement beneficiaries on the first business day of each month and logs the review.

Compensating control (one-person business): the owner is the only administrator, so the logs stay with the vendors. The custodian portal, email suite, CRM, and portfolio platform keep their sign-in and activity logs on their own platforms. Limit: the email plan keeps sign-in history for only 30 days, so the forwarding rule found 2026-07-15 could not be traced further back.
evidence: Vendor admin consoles; SOC 2 report for SYS-02 (P09)

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the P07 plan states openly that independence is limited, because the owner designed, operates, and assessed the controls with help from the on-call IT consultant. POL-01 4.5 requires review by someone outside the business, such as the IT consultant, at least every second year. The portfolio platform vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report, reviewed 2026-07-16, covers that vendor's inherited controls. Gap: the first outside review has not taken place.
evidence: P07 assessment plan; POL-01 4.5; P09 review

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): there is no change board, so under CM-3(g) the owner is the change control element. POL-01 4.7 requires every security-relevant setting change and every new tool to be written in the security log with the date and reason. POL-01 4.3 requires a risk assessment update after any material change, such as a new system or vendor.

The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gap: no arrangement for another adviser to act if the owner is incapacitated, and no sealed emergency access sheet (due 2026-12-31).

The custodian holds the records of account, and each SaaS vendor backs up its own service (inherited). Owner responsibility: email and files keep only 30 days of versions; a weekly copy goes to a USB drive that is not encrypted and is plugged into the laptop while it copies.
evidence: Suite retention settings; USB drive check (P07)

implementation_statement: The owner holds administrator rights in the email tenant, CRM, portfolio platform, e-signature, and accounting services. The vendors offer MFA, but it is off on all five. Owner turns it on by 2026-09-15 and registers a hardware key as a second method.

The owner's non-administrator accounts (the custodian portal user login used for trading and money movement, and the financial planning software) require an authenticator app, enforced by those vendors. The owner's other accounts are administrator accounts and are covered by IA-2(1).
The email password is reused on two other sites and other passwords follow one pattern. Planned: a password manager with unique passphrases of at least 14 characters by 2026-09-15.
No list of whom to tell or by when. Planned: the P08 notification matrix (custodian fraud desk, counsel, Florida notices, FTC if 500 or more consumers).

The business email compromise runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-08-31. A written plan is not required at this size (314.6 exempts 314.4(h)); the owner adopted one anyway because Florida's 30-day clock needs one. Gap: not yet walked through (due 2026-09-30).
Paper goes through the cross-cut shredder. Gap: no procedure for wiping old laptops, phones, and drives; an old laptop from 2021 is still in a closet.
The home office door locks and paper client files are in a locked cabinet. Gap: the USB backup drive sits in an unlocked desk drawer.

First risk assessment completed 2026-07-17 using NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). A written assessment is not required at this size (314.6), but the program must be based on one (314.4(b)). Reviewed each July and after material changes.

The custodian and SaaS vendors are under their standard terms; the email suite and portfolio platform terms include security commitments, and the IT consultant signed security terms on 2026-07-10. Gap: no vendor list, no review of the CRM, e-signature, or AI vendors, and no security terms with the compliance consultant.
evidence: Vendor contracts folder; SOC 2 report for SYS-02

implementation_statement: The laptop host firewall is on. Gap: one home network is shared with family and smart-home devices, and the router admin password was never changed. A separate business network is planned by 2026-12-31.
All SaaS traffic uses TLS (inherited). Gap: client documents go to the compliance consultant and some clients as ordinary email attachments.
SaaS vendors encrypt data at rest (inherited for SYS-02 per its SOC 2 report). The laptop and phone are encrypted. Gap: the USB backup drive holding every client folder is not encrypted.
Vendors patch their services. Automatic updates are on for the laptop and phone. Gap noted under SC-7: router firmware has never been checked.
Built-in antivirus runs real-time scans with automatic updates. Owner keeps it on and acts on alerts.
Books and records are kept as the Florida OFR requires (Fla. Stat. 517.121), but there is no written retention and disposal schedule. Former-client records back to 2015 are kept in every system.
